name: Varun Beverages Ltd
title: Varun Beverages Ltd - 540180 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: India volume +22.5% in Q3 with realisation only +0.5%, while packaging cost hit ~300 bps of gross margin; management says gross margin likely troughed this quarter, though 20%+ India growth prior guidance was not explicitly restated with numbers.

summary.headline: VBL Q3 CY2026 revenue rose 33.2% to Rs 66,076 mn, with gross margin down 334 bps to 53.1% on packaging cost inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 33.2% YoY to Rs 66,076 mn and EBITDA rose 25.1% to Rs 14,267 mn, with EBITDA margin at 21.6% (down 140 bps). Volume growth was 28.7% consolidated, with India at 22.5% and international at 39.9%. Gross margin fell 334 bps to 53.1% as packaging inflation from the geopolitical conflict (around 300 bps) and a surge in lower-margin preform and cap sales (about 100 bps in India) weighed. Management said gross margin has likely troughed at current prices, and it announced an interim dividend of Rs 0.50 per share and a KIVA Spirits entry into alcobev/RTD.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume grew 22.5% in Q3; realisation per case rose 0.5%. EBITDA margin was broadly stable YoY in 9M CY2026 despite input cost pressure. Low/no-sugar share rose to 88% from 44% a year ago.

segments.name: International (Africa)
segments.commentary: Volume grew 39.9% in Q3, with realisation up on South Africa pricing and FX. International gross margin pressure was about 272 bps versus about 300 bps in India. Twizza merged with BevCo effective 1 Aug 2026.

segments.name: Product mix (volume, Q3)
segments.commentary: CSD 73.3%, juice-based drinks 4.8%, packaged water 21.9% of sales volume. Non-beverage sales (preforms, caps) in India rose about 104%.

guidance_outlook: Management said gross margin has broadly troughed in Q3 CY2026 at current price trends, barring new macro surprises.
Upside to margins could come from price-pack architecture changes, following the Sting pack downsize from 300 ml to 250 ml.
Management said more than half of the 3-4% gross margin impact has been mitigated through cost reductions.
International capex is about USD 90-100 mn; India capex is about Rs 1,000 crore, including a greenfield plant at Suratgarh, Rajasthan and a PET line. CY2026 capex is complete.
Management plans to add about 100,000 outlets a year from the current 4.2 mn, and is aggressively planning numeric and weighted distribution for CY2027.
Calpis launch is planned for December-January, with a broader marketing calendar around late February or March.
capex_capacity: Capacity is full in most African markets; Morocco capacity is short ahead of its season and new lines are planned in Morocco, Zimbabwe and DRC.
South Africa and DRC seasons run November to January with plants at full speed; Twizza gives enough South African capacity this year.
Zimbabwe has a capacity gap that Zambia will partly cover from this month, and more capacity is being added next year.
rPET is about 25% of PET needs via in-house backward integration; the next rPET plant is expected to be operational within 1-2 quarters.
Capex across India and international markets is roughly Rs 1,000 crore and USD 90 mn respectively.
demand_pricing: India volume growth is 22.5%, and 9M India growth is about 16-17%; management said volume growth has been positive since May.
No list-price increase on CSD in Q3; realisation gains came from mix, premium launches (Ad Rush, Evervess mixers), calibrated discounting and price-pack architecture.

Sting pack reduced from 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June to offset raw-material costs. Energy category volumes were hit by an FSSAI labelling ruling; management estimated negativity at about 25% mid-quarter and said Sting is now recovering.
Rs 10 price point is about 0.2-0.3% of volume; management will not push it because unit economics do not work at 150 ml.
Africa: Mondelez exclusive distribution agreement in Zimbabwe (Mondelez has about USD 11 mn existing business there). Kenya beverage operations started with BOLT UP and XTREME FIZZ.
Management said October is still in progress and declined to comment on October trends.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for gross margins next quarter and March quarter, and split of packaging, sugar and non-beverage impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the packaging cost hit applies from purchases after the war began around 28 Feb; the company was covered for one quarter. It said the sugar impact was offset by low/no-sugar mix, and the 3-4% gross margin impact is more than half mitigated.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 gross margin the trough?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yes, broadly, at present price trends, with upside from price-pack changes. The pace of roll-down to other packs will determine that upside.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a sugar or packaging price increase on CSD, and when?
qa_highlights.answer: No CSD price increase was taken in Q3; the only pack change was Sting 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the crude/PET cost increase is in the P&L?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 100% impact of crude is already built in, and rPET (about 25% of PET) has helped contain costs.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new entrant part of the beverage association discussing price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no common forum; industry chatter is about price-pack and trade margin responses if costs stay high.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan for CY27 and split?
qa_highlights.answer: CY2026 capex is complete. CY27 is about Rs 1,000 crore for India (including Suratgarh greenfield and a PET line) and USD 90-100 mn for international.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for KIVA Spirits and alcobev?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early days and is in talks with global partners, focusing on RTDs (growing 13-15%) and premium alcobev with no margin-dilutive portfolios. It is open to inorganic options.

risks_watch: Packaging and crude-linked cost inflation: gross margin pressure of about 300 bps persists, and management could not give specific Q4 guidance.
Non-beverage sales (preforms, caps) rose about 104% and cut gross margin by about 100 bps in India; sustainability is unclear.
Energy category recovery after the FSSAI labelling ruling; Sting volumes are recovering but not yet at baseline.
Competitive price-pack response by the industry, or trade margin cuts, if raw material costs stay high.
Finance costs rose 53.5% and depreciation 34.5% after the Twizza acquisition and debt funding.
Africa capacity constraints in Zimbabwe and Morocco ahead of the next season; FX volatility.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and the India recovery, but cautious on the margin outlook. Management repeatedly declined to give forward margin or October trend numbers, citing the uncertain geopolitical situation and fuel prices.
key_quotes: Higher packaging costs weighed on margins during the quarter, although improved realizations and operating leverage from strong volume growth helped partially offset these pressures.
Based upon the present price trends, we can broadly say yes. We hope there are no more surprises on the macro factors.
The 100% impact of crude price is already built in because all these fresh stocks are being consumed.
Quarter is still in progress, Anand. We think we should wait.

New lines in Morocco, Zimbabwe and DRC (International; part of ~USD 90-100 mn capex for CY27)
Next rPET plant (in-house PET backward integration)
Zambia capacity covering Zimbabwe gap, from this month

growth.why: Management guides to India growth of 20-plus% run-rate with high double-digit ambition for FY27, backed by India volume +22.5% in Q3, 9M India growth ~16-17%, Zambia capacity from this month, and new lines/plants in Morocco, Zimbabwe, DRC and Suratgarh, though no specific revenue growth number is guided and capacity timing is mostly unspecified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said gross margin has broadly troughed and more than half of the 3-4% hit is mitigated, but upside depends on the pace of Sting and other pack roll-downs and on the packaging and crude path, which management would not forecast.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Zambia from Nov 2026; Suratgarh and PET line Q2-Q4 FY27 window
rows.why: Zambia capacity covering Zimbabwe gap starts this month, Suratgarh greenfield plus PET line (part of ~Rs 1,000 cr India capex) is under construction, and new Morocco, Zimbabwe and DRC lines are planned for CY27 with ~USD 90-100 mn capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India volume grew 22.5% in Q3 and has been positive since May, international volume grew 39.9%, and the company plans about 100,000 outlets a year added to 4.2 mn, so volume growth is guided to continue.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: CY27 capex is already guided at ~Rs 1,000 cr India and USD 90-100 mn international, and management said Morocco capacity is short and Zimbabwe has a gap, so capacity additions are not in doubt.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: India growth is running at 22.5% in Q3 with 9M India growth at about 16-17%, and management said it is happy with 20-plus% growth, but it did not raise any numeric guide.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Packaging and crude-linked inflation keeps about 300 bps of gross margin pressure in place, and management gave no specific Q4 guidance, though it said Q3 is the likely trough at current prices.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Calpis launch is planned for December-January with a broader marketing calendar around late February or March, and KIVA Spirits is in early talks for RTD and premium alcobev.

rows.label: Kenya beverage operations and Zimbabwe Mondelez distribution
rows.why: Kenya operations started with BOLT UP and XTREME FIZZ, and Mondelez has an exclusive Zimbabwe distribution agreement where Mondelez already has about USD 11 mn of business.

rows.label: Sting pack downsize and price-pack architecture
rows.why: Sting moved from 300 ml to 250 ml around May-June, and management said upside to margins depends on the pace of pack roll-down to other packs, with no CSD list price hike taken in Q3.

rows.label: rPET plant commissioning
rows.why: The next rPET plant is expected to be operational within 1-2 quarters, and rPET already covers about 25% of PET needs through in-house backward integration.

tone.note: Management was confident on India volume recovery, Africa capacity and the trough in gross margin, but declined to give forward margin or October trend numbers, and analysts pushed on packaging and crude pass-through and on the sustainability of the non-beverage sales surge.
